title: Trek to the copper-tinted water of Arroyo Turquesa
description: Make the six-hour return hike to a mineral-coloured stream near Cerro Mercedario at almost 4,000 metres. Go acclimatised and confirm mountain conditions with a local guide.

title: Cross the petrified white waves of Campo de Piedra Pómez
description: Travel with a local high-altitude guide into a protected field of pale volcanic stone more than 3,000 metres above sea level. Wind has sculpted the rock into an uncanny frozen sea.

title: Walk the red slot canyons of the Cuevas de Acsibi
description: Ride by 4WD from near Seclantás, then hike roughly four hours through narrow red formations and past Kakán rock art. Entry requires a specialist guide.

title: Drive among the black cones of La Payunia volcanic reserve
description: Join an authorised excursion into a remote reserve of hundreds of volcanic cones, dark lava slopes and red-black ridges. The protected landscape sits about 300 kilometres from Mendoza city.

title: Explore Somuncurá's volcanic plateau with local baqueanos
description: Cross the isolated Patagonian steppe by 4WD with local route knowledge, then walk or ride across a volcanic tableland dotted with seasonal lagoons. Access is weather-dependent and services are sparse.

title: Camp beneath the forest sky at Salto Encantado
description: Follow forest viewpoints around a 64-metre waterfall, then stay for the park's small-scale camping and occasional Guaraní sky interpretation. Confirm the astronomy programme before travelling.

title: Hike with a guide to the Río Jordán thermal pools
description: Walk through Yungas forest to mineral-rich blue-green pools warmed to around 30°C. Visits require a guide, and river and trail conditions should be checked locally.

title: Reach the solitary cone of Arita on the high salt flat
description: Cross the high-altitude Salar de Arizaro with a local driver to see a near-perfect 200-metre volcanic-and-salt cone rising from the plain. Carry cold-weather gear despite the stark desert setting.

title: See mineral colours ring the Salto del Agrio
description: Walk to the rim where the Agrio River drops more than 80 metres into an ochre amphitheatre. Iron and sulphur tint the water and surrounding rock red, yellow and green.

title: Soak beside geysers in Sajama National Park
description: Explore Sajama's high-altitude geothermal field and thermal water beneath Bolivia's highest peak. Register with park staff, use a local guide and prepare for cold, wind and altitude.

title: Travel by river into Manuripi wildlife reserve
description: Arrange a guided river journey into a nationally protected Amazon reserve promoted as a developing nature destination. Confirm permits, transport and seasonal access before departure.

title: Enter Amboró's cloud forest with a registered guide
description: Approach the protected ecological corridor from the Samaipata side for guided walks in cloud forest and foothills. Access varies by sector, so arrange a registered guide and current park advice.

title: Swim below the Saltos waterfalls in the Cerrado
description: Hike through Chapada dos Veadeiros to a series of falls and natural pools. The official tourism board identifies the dry months from April to October as the most reliable period for local adventure travel.

title: Walk water-carved rock at Vale da Lua
description: Follow the trail to smooth, water-sculpted rock channels that resemble a lunar surface. Check rainfall and local restrictions because water levels can transform the formations quickly.

title: Hike to the framed horizon at Mirante da Janela
description: Climb through open Cerrado and rock formations to a natural window overlooking the Chapada horizon. Start early, carry water and use marked local access.

title: Visit Santa Bárbara waterfall with the Kalunga community
description: Walk through native vegetation to a turquoise waterfall near the Chapada park, arranging the visit through the local Kalunga area. Capacity and guide rules should be confirmed before travel.

title: Hike to the lip of Cachoeira da Fumaça
description: Take the high trail to a waterfall dropping roughly 390 metres from the Chapada plateau. Flow changes seasonally, so confirm conditions and carry enough water for exposed sections.

title: Enter the long limestone passages of Lapa Doce
description: Walk a guided section of a cave system extending for about 25 kilometres beneath Chapada Diamantina. Use an authorised local guide and do not assume every passage is open.

title: Paddle the flooded forest of Marimbus
description: Canoe or kayak across a broad wetland of rivers and aquatic plants, often starting near Remanso and continuing toward the Roncador River. Arrange the route locally because water conditions vary.

title: Share a wetland journey from the Remanso quilombola community
description: Begin a locally arranged Marimbus journey from a quilombola community reached by dirt road. Keep the visit community-led and pair the wetland trip with an introduction to local history.

title: Boulder on the old diamond paths above Igatu
description: Climb with a qualified local guide in Igatu's Serra Alta or Califórnia sectors, then trace stonework left by the diamond era. This is technical rock terrain, not an unguided sightseeing stop.

title: Walk among old-growth trees in Alerce Andino
description: Take a forest trail in one of the quieter northern parks on Chile's 17-park Patagonian route. Expect rain even in summer and confirm trail status with CONAF.

title: Hike between fjords and forest in Hornopirén
description: Explore a remote park of temperate forest, lakes and steep terrain along the Patagonian Parks Route. Public transport is limited, and route and weather checks are essential.

title: Walk the forest trails of Pumalín Douglas Tompkins
description: Link short forest walks and volcanic viewpoints in a park on Chile's long Patagonian route. Allow extra time for ferry and road disruptions and check individual trail openings.

title: Climb to the turquoise lagoon below Cerro Castillo
description: Tackle a steep Patagonian day hike to the lagoon beneath the castle-like ridge. Wind and fast weather changes make current park guidance and proper mountain equipment essential.

title: Watch guanacos cross Patagonia National Park
description: Walk or drive slowly through the Chacabuco Valley for open-steppe wildlife and broad mountain views. It is one of 17 parks on a route with limited transport in its most isolated sections.

title: Follow the Sierra Nevada trail above Conguillío's lava fields
description: Climb through ancient araucaria forest above volcanic lagoons and Llaima's lava landscape. Roads are largely gravel and winter access can require 4WD.

title: Hike to Selkirk's Lookout across Robinson Crusoe Island
description: Cross native island forest to a high pass with views to both coasts. Reaching Robinson Crusoe Island itself requires a charter flight and boat transfer, so reserve well ahead.

title: Walk with local guides to the Cerro Azul pictographs
description: Travel from San José del Guaviare with a local guide to rock shelters covered in ancient painted figures. Follow current community, conservation and security advice.

title: Walk beneath the sandstone span of Puerta de Orión
description: Follow a locally guided trail through the Guaviare's old sandstone landscape to a freestanding natural portal. Confirm road, rain and security conditions before leaving San José.

title: Paddle quietly into Laguna Negra
description: Take a community-arranged canoe excursion on a dark-water lagoon near San José del Guaviare. Keep noise low for wildlife and check wet-season access locally.

title: Climb the granite dome of Cerro de Mavecure
description: Journey by river from Inírida and climb ancient granite with Indigenous community guidance. The remote logistics and local access arrangements make this a planned expedition.

title: Boat the Orinoco rapids of El Tuparro
description: Arrange an authorised journey into remote Orinoco savanna and river country, where granite outcrops break the current. Check park access and regional security immediately before travel.

title: Walk the former prison island trails of Gorgona
description: Reach this offshore national park by authorised boat, then follow rainforest trails around former prison remains and rich marine habitat. Sea conditions and park rules determine access.

title: Paddle and walk with community guides at Añangu
description: Combine canoe travel, forest walks, wildlife watching and cultural interpretation at an approved Yasuní visitor site. Use an authorised operator and respect community protocols.

title: Watch river-edge wildlife at Tambococha
description: Visit one of Yasuní's designated sites for guided canoeing, walking and flora-and-fauna observation. Entry and exit hours are controlled, so travel only through an authorised itinerary.

title: Explore the forest around Indillama by canoe and foot
description: Move between river and rainforest at a low-volume designated Yasuní visitor site. Keep the experience guide-led and confirm the permitted route before departure.

title: Join a small community visit at Nueva Providencia
description: Arrange cultural interpretation, canoeing and wildlife observation at an official Yasuní visitor site. Treat the community as host, not scenery, and follow the operator's access window.

title: Canoe to the forest site of Mandaripanga
description: Use a permitted Yasuní operator for a river-and-forest day at this designated visitor location. Wildlife sightings are never guaranteed and park timing rules apply.

title: Camp by Jatuncocha lagoon with advance park approval
description: Stay beside a remote Yasuní lagoon only through an operator that has requested the required advance camping reservation. Pack for humidity and strict low-impact travel.

title: Kayak among Huancaya's stepped emerald lagoons
description: Stay at least two days in Huancaya to walk, paddle or ride beside small waterfalls and green lagoons in the landscape reserve. The overland trip from Lima is long.

title: Walk through winter-green hills at Lomas de Lúcumo
description: Choose a three-to-six-hour community trail through seasonal vegetation, rock art and wildlife habitat outside Lima. The hills are at their greenest from June to November.

title: Camp among the strange stone figures of Marcahuasi
description: Carry cold-weather camping equipment onto an Andean plateau of weathered rock formations above San Pedro de Casta. Altitude and low night temperatures demand preparation.

title: Walk the mist-fed trails of Lachay reserve
description: Follow a choice of walking circuits through coastal hills transformed by winter mist, watching for foxes and seasonal flowers. June to October brings the richest green cover.

title: Walk the painted village streets of Antioquía
description: Explore a small Andean town whose white buildings carry bright painted borders, flowers and animals, then walk to local viewpoints or fruit fields. It is roughly three hours from Lima.

title: Look across fruit orchards from Azpitia
description: Pause in a rural fruit-growing district above the Mala River valley, pairing the viewpoint with a slow local meal or short country walk. It is a low-key diversion south of Lima.

title: Soak in the Tumac springs outside Cajatambo
description: Make the long mountain journey to cobbled Cajatambo, then walk locally to warm springs in the surrounding valley. Verify road and facility conditions before setting out.

title: Climb to the stone citadel of Rúpac
description: Travel through Huaral and Pampas, then hike to high stone ruins above the cloud line. Camp only with local advice and carry warm layers and water.

title: Watch flamingos at the Campo María salt lagoon
description: Visit a salt lagoon and conservation refuge on Paraguay's Chaco-and-Pantanal route for dry-forest and wetland birdlife. Arrange local access and take supplies for heat and isolation.

title: Walk with Guaraní hosts in the Mbaracayú forest
description: Arrange a small-scale forest and cultural visit in one of the remaining Alto Paraná Atlantic Forest landscapes. Use community-approved guides and respect local access conditions.

title: Descend the gorge trail at Quebrada de los Cuervos
description: Follow a marked trail into a narrow gorge cut by the Yerbal Chico stream, through unusually lush eastern hill vegetation. Check the current booking and guide rules before arriving.

title: Follow the Tembetarí interpretive trail in Villa Serrana
description: Walk a 1.6-kilometre interpretive route through hill forest, fungi and streams near Cerro Pelado. The two-hour experience can be guided and is deliberately small-scale.

title: Walk the machinery floor of the former Anglo works
place: Museum of the Industrial Revolution, Fray Bentos
description: Tour the renewed museum inside a former meat-processing complex that reshaped global food production. The machinery and workers' landscape give a tangible view of industrial history.

title: Stay with the Makushi community at Rewa Village
description: Reach a community-owned lodge at the meeting of the Rewa and Rupununi rivers for guided fishing, wildlife and forest experiences. The journey requires internal flights, boats or 4WD transfers.

title: Boat between rainforest islands and colonial forts on the Essequibo
description: Arrange a licensed river guide to link small islands, forest banks and surviving fort sites on Guyana's largest river. Distances and currents make this a planned boat day.

title: Boat into Bigi Pan for scarlet ibis and flamingos
description: Use a local boat guide to enter the protected western wetland, watching ibis, flamingos and mangrove wildlife from the lagoon. Current government work highlights unresolved management issues, so verify operator and access arrangements.

title: Walk the forest loop of the Sentier des Géants
description: Follow a roughly three-hour park-marked circuit past giant rainforest trees and a rocky creek outside Maripasoula. Check the evolving track condition with the park or tourism office first.

title: Travel by pirogue and foot to Gobaya Soula falls
description: Ride about 20 minutes upriver from Maripasoula, then walk a maintained forest trail to local swimming falls on the Atachi Baaka foothills. Arrange transport and current advice locally.

title: Hike to the Falklands' highest summit, Mount Usborne
description: Climb to the 705-metre high point of the islands for wide views across East Falkland. Arrange land access, tell someone your route and carry strong boots and layered clothing.

title: Walk the coast to Cape Pembroke Lighthouse
description: Take the roughly three-hour walk to the archipelago's easternmost lighthouse through ponds, coves and exposed coast. Check land access and the countryside code before setting out.
